target: Mac daily-use polish: single window, native commands, scheduled mini timer, and metadata library

contract.purpose: Help a person plan a realistic day, follow the current intention, capture what changes it, and learn why the day lived differed from the day planned.
contract.purposeSource: PRODUCT.md and site-health projects.anchor purpose contract
contract.canonicalPurpose: Anchor helps a person plan a realistic day, keep the current intention visible, capture what changes it, and learn why the lived day differed from the plan.
contract.audience: A private owner who plans and focuses from a Mac and expects the app to behave like a polished native utility throughout the workday.
contract.job: Make the next planned action immediately startable, keep the timer reachable without context switching, and make reusable project and tag context trustworthy to edit.
contract.thesis: Preserve The Drawn Day while making Mac structure quieter and more native: one window, discoverable menus, a schedule-aware mini timer, and calm editable libraries.
contract.system: Existing neutral paper and charcoal surfaces, SF typography, one ink action, Anchor spacing and radii, native Mac menus and fields, and authored colour only for meaningful project or interruption context.
contract.signature: The scheduled intention moves directly from Today into the menu-bar timer, so Anchor stays present without pulling the owner out of their work.
contract.risk: Adding capability to the mini timer could make it noisy; scheduled context is limited to one current or next block and yields to the existing compact composer.

projectCheck.command: rtk swift test && xcodebuildmcp macos build --scheme Anchor (macOS) --configuration DebugLocal

findings: Native SwiftUI surface; browser UI detector is not applicable.

ownerFeedback.note: The owner directed a Mac-only preserve pass and clarified the core: maintain habits, sort the calendar, start and stop focus, and review focus hours and blockers. No scope expansion was taken.
